entry.title: The Power of Solitude
entry.content:
“Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured.”

I. The Art of Solitude

In this fast-paced and noisy world, we are often taught to be sociable. But after the noise fades, have you ever felt the peace and power of being alone?

For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone—for both our work lives and our emotional well-being. Learning to love your solitude is an essential lesson in life.

II. The Source of Creativity

Many creative individuals are often less interested in socializing. In fact, Deist’s research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialism.

Many artists are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they are trying to give expression and meaning to through their art. Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process. A paper by Booker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect—they found that creativity was linked specifically to accountability.

III. Mental Rest and Focus

One benefit of accountability is the brain’s state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone. When another person is present, your brain can’t help but pay some attention. This can be a positive distraction. But it’s still a distraction.

Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialize once more. And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.

IV. Charting Our Own Path

Humans are such absorbent social beings that when we surround ourselves with others, we automatically take in their opinions and aesthetics. Therefore, to truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time.

It’s hard to examine one’s own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude. In addition, introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships—which has been linked to greater happiness. Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you.

V. Conclusion

As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. Just as I mentioned in my first blog, “See the world, see others, see yourself.” Solitude is exactly the path to “seeing yourself.”

The best state of life is perhaps not always seeking validation in the crowd, but having the ability to step back at any time and have a dialogue with oneself. Drawing strength from solitude and radiating warmth in socializing—this is probably the most clear-headed way to live.

Reference Source: The ideas and quotes in this article are primarily derived from the paragraph matching section of the CET-6 (College English Test Band 6) exam in June 2025, titled “The Benefits of Solitude”.

The third post on this site, written on October 10, 2026, in Hefei, Anhui.
entry.summary: Reflections on life and the benefits of being alone.

entry.title: 忽闻桂花香，方知秋已至

link.title: 忽闻桂花香，方知秋已至

entry.content:
“忽闻桂花香，方知秋已至，又是一年桂花开，半生风雨自徘徊。”

一、秋雨落合肥，金粟坠清涟

我来到了满城尽是桂花香的城市。

一场秋雨过后，碎桂沾湿径，暗香随风漫。一城秋意，尽在这桂雨之间。

此刻的合肥，一阵浓郁而熟悉的香气扑面而来，桂花落地，满城秋香。

二、欲买桂花同载酒，终不似，少年游

驻足在满地的金黄前，突然想起那句诗：欲买桂花同载酒，终不似，少年游。

好像什么都来得及，又好像什么都无能为力。

桂花每年都会如期而至，但赏花的心境却一年不同于一年。年少时的秋游，是纯粹的兴奋与欢喜；如今的秋思，却夹杂着对未来的迷茫。我们终于长到了能“买桂花同载酒”的年纪，却再也找不回那份纯粹的少年心气。

三、写在最后

见天地，方知寒来暑往，秋收冬藏。

这一场合肥的桂花雨，让我看到了季节的更替。

如果这篇小文让你也想出门走走，不妨去合肥植物园看看最全的桂花品种，去逍遥津公园闻一闻古战场旁的秋香，或者沿着长江西路的金桂大道走一段——那条路以金桂为行道树，花开时满路金黄，是城市里一条“闻得到”的桂花走廊。

本站第二篇文章，写于 2026 年 10 月 3 日，安徽合肥。
entry.summary: 合肥秋雨后，满城桂花香。

entry.title: 见天地，见众生，见自己
entry.content:
万千繁华，不过三种风景：见天地，见众生，见自己。

一、见天地

见天地，方知寒来暑往，秋收冬藏，感受天高无穷，体悟自身渺小，如沧海一粟。

天地是规律，阴晴圆缺，生老病死。

二、见众生

见众生，人性百态徐徐展开，虽人心难测，如神明不可探，却知众生皆有所因。

众生是人性，妖魔鬼怪，名利权情。

三、见自己

见自己，看到贪嗔痴恨，七情六欲，在真我本我面前，学会敬畏、豁达与宽容。内心平静，万籁俱寂，再无纷扰能够影响。

自己是欲望，七情六欲，贪嗔痴念。

四、写在最后

人是未来佛，佛是过来人。

于天地间感悟规律，于众生中洞察事相，于自我处寻找安宁，此乃人生之境也。

  • 见天地，知敬畏，所以谦卑；
  • 见众生，懂怜悯，所以宽容；
  • 见自己，明归途，所以豁达。

本站第一篇文章，写于 2026 年 10 月 1 日，安徽合肥。
entry.summary: 第一篇博客，记录对人生三见的思考。
